_readme: IntMap · submarine-cable reconstruction — the CORRECTIONS, as data.
scripts/build-subcables.mjs reads this file. Nothing here may be a latitude/longitude
written into code instead: every hand-made decision about the cable dataset lives in this
one file so that re-running the pipeline reproduces it (the brief's §20).
nameAliases      normalized source spelling -> normalized TeleGeography spelling. Applied by
scripts/subcables/match.mjs BEFORE any comparison. Keys and values are
lower-case, punctuation collapsed to single spaces.
pieceCable       '<src>|<name>' -> TeleGeography cable id, or null to refuse the piece.
An explicit answer for a case the name+place test cannot settle by itself.
A null is a DECISION, and the QA counts them, so a source route that is
deliberately not used cannot look like one that was never seen.
anchors          cable id -> extra waypoints the reconstruction must pass through, in order,
as [lon, lat]. For legs where the published route is known to go somewhere
the sea floor alone would not send it. Each entry MUST carry a `why`.
channels         waterways narrower than one 1/12° cell (9.26 km) that cables really transit.
The router carves them into its passability at `cost` (they are shallow and
busy, not free). Each MUST carry a `why`, and the build reports how many
cells each one opened so a channel that does nothing cannot hide.
rivers           rivers that named cable systems are laid IN. The elevation grid has no river
in it, so these legs had no water to route over at all. The COURSE is not
written here: it is taken from Natural Earth's 1:10m river centre lines (the
public-domain source the lakes already come from), selected by name AND bbox
because a name alone does not identify a river ('Negro' is four rivers, three
of them in Argentina and Uruguay). Each MUST carry a `why`, and the build
reports the features matched and the cells opened.
excludeSources   normalized source names that are not telecom cable systems at all.
countryCodes     TeleGeography country spelling -> ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, for the spellings CLDR
does not use. The card translates COUNTRIES THROUGH THE CODE (CLDR already
holds every ISO region in all nine languages), so this table is the join key
and NOT a translation: 8 entries, not 186 x 9 strings. scripts/subcables/
regions.mjs resolves the other 178 from CLDR itself and the build prints any
spelling that reaches no code, which then stays English rather than guessed.

channels.name: Suez Canal
channels.why: The canal is ~200 m wide and the grid cell is 9.26 km, so the Red Sea and the Mediterranean are two separate oceans to the router. Measured on the raw grid: Port Said -> Suez routed 25,141 km around Africa for a 151 km leg, and that single blockage is what made Red2Med 117x, EMC West-1 13.9x, India-Europe Xpress 6.0x and MENA/GBI 7.0x their published lengths. Cables transiting Egypt (SeaMeWe-3/4/5/6, IMEWE, AAE-1, PEACE, 2Africa, FALCON, EIG, TE North, Africa-1 ...) really are laid through the canal and its terminal lakes.

channels.name: Bosphorus + Sea of Marmara + Dardanelles
channels.why: The Bosphorus is 0.7-3.4 km and the Dardanelles 1.2-6 km, so the Black Sea has no connection to the Mediterranean on this grid (measured: Istanbul north -> south, NO ROUTE). Cables between the Black Sea and the Aegean are laid through both straits.

rivers.name: Amazonas
rivers.why: Norte Conectado Infovia 00/01/02/03 and Projeto Amazônia Conectada PAC-01 are laid in the Amazon and the Solimões — Macapá/Santarém/Óbidos/Parintins/Manaus/Tefé/Tabatinga are river towns, not sea ports. Measured on the 1/12° grid before this: every one of those legs was UNROUTABLE and came out as a geodesic across the rainforest (Infovia-05 alone put 273 sampled points on land). The Natural Earth centre line passes within 3-7 km of Tabatinga, Tefé and Fonte Boa.

rivers.name: Negro
rivers.why: Projeto Amazônia Conectada PAC-02 runs Manaus - Novo Airão - Moura - Barcelos - Santa Isabel - São Gabriel da Cachoeira, which is the Rio Negro from mouth to upper reach; Norte Conectado Infovia-04 joins it at Moura. The centre line passes 2-11 km from all six. The bbox is what separates this from the Río Negro of Argentina and the Río Negro of Uruguay, which carry the same name in the same dataset.

rivers.name: Branco
rivers.why: Norte Conectado Infovia-04 is Boa Vista - Caracaraí - Santa Maria do Boiaçu - Moura, which is the Rio Branco down to its confluence with the Negro. Centre line within 2-4 km of Boa Vista and Caracaraí.

rivers.name: Madeira
rivers.why: Norte Conectado Infovia-05 is Porto Velho - Humaitá - Calama - Manicoré - Novo Aripuanã - Borba - Autazes, the Rio Madeira from Porto Velho to the Amazon. This is the cable #R355 measured at 6,287 km against a published 1,116 km when the snap was unbounded, and at 1,768 km of pure geodesic once it was bounded. Centre line within 2 km of Porto Velho, Humaitá and Borba.

rivers.name: Juruá
rivers.why: Norte Conectado Infovia-08 is Cruzeiro do Sul - Fonte Boa, which is the Rio Juruá end to end. Centre line within 1 km of Cruzeiro do Sul and 4 km of Fonte Boa.

countryCodes._why: The other 178 spellings the inventory uses resolve straight from CLDR's own English region names (scripts/subcables/regions.mjs). These eight do not, because CLDR spells them differently, and every one is a NAME difference and not a territory difference — checked one by one against ISO 3166-1.
